newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France seeks lowest feasible EU cereals set-aside.
newsitem.headline: France seeks lowest feasible EU cereals set-aside.

text.p: France's new farm minister Louis Le Pensec has urged Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to propose that the 1998 cereals set-aside rate should be set as low as possible, a European Commission spokesman said on Friday.
"Ideally (for France) it would be zero but the minister was not specific," the spokesman said, adding that Fischler made no commitment.
Fischler wants to have a clearer picture of harvest prospects before submitting a proposal next month.
The current rate for compulsory set-aside is five percent.
Commission officials noted that when the 1997 set-aside rate was fixed last July, the 1996 harvest was estimated at 187 million tonnes. The final total was 201 million tonnes.
Fischler will be pressed at an EU farm ministers meeting in Luxembourg next week to rapidly recommend a rate so that it can be agreed at the July EU Farm Council.
Although some member states, such as Germany and Austria, have traditionally sought a high rate, officials said that a consensus was forming around keeping the five percent figure.
Le Pensec also rejected a proposal to cut aid payments to cereals and oilseed farmers.
But the French minister added during a first meeting with Fischler that a reduction could be discussed in the context of future farm reforms, the spokesman said.
Fischler has called for a 1.4 billion ecus cut in cereals and oilseeds compensatory payments to help finance aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.
The proposal, which is opposed by all EU countries except Britain and Sweden, is attached to the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package which is due to be agreed by EU farm ministers next week.
